messages:
rachel: Hi all, first-day annoyance. My app inside docker-compose keeps getting ECONNREFUSED to postgres:5432. The postgres container is healthy and `docker-compose ps` shows it running. I'm on mac + Docker Desktop. Any ideas?

ben: Welcome! Can you paste your compose service snippets and the DB URL?

rachel: Sure: ```
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: pass
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL","pg_isready -U postgres"]
      interval: 5s
  web:
    build: .
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:pass@postgres:5432/dev
    depends_on:
      - postgres
    extra_hosts:
      - "postgres:127.0.0.1"
```

marco: Whoa, `extra_hosts` mapping postgres to 127.0.0.1 will force the web container to resolve the hostname `postgres` to the container's own loopback, not the actual postgres container. That makes the TCP handshake go to the web container itself -> ECONNREFUSED.

ben: Exactly. Remove that extra_hosts entry. It was probably added to make host tooling resolve `postgres` to localhost for some other reason, but inside the docker network you should rely on service DNS.

rachel: I inherited the compose file from a coworker who wanted `psql -h postgres` to work from mac host. They probably thought extra_hosts was the right approach. Any safe way to allow host->container name resolution without breaking inter-container DNS?

marco: Two safer options: 1) publish the postgres port (e.g., `ports: - "5432:5432"`) and use `localhost` from your Mac host to connect; or 2) add an entry in your /etc/hosts on the host machine that maps `postgres.local` to 127.0.0.1 and run a tiny proxy, but don't clobber the container DNS. If you must, you can use `docker run --network host` on Linux, but on mac/Colima/Docker Desktop that doesn't behave the same.

ben: For local dev it's simplest to remove the extra_hosts, set `DATABASE_URL` to `postgres:5432` (service name), and publish the port if you also need host access. Also add a healthcheck and small retry in web start so migrations wait.

rachel: Removed the extra_hosts and changed nothing else. App connects instantly and migrations run. Phew! Thanks for spotting the weird mapping.

infra-bot: Dev docs updated with a short note about avoiding extra_hosts collisions for service names and recommended patterns for host vs container DNS: https://redwood-inference.internal/docs/dev-setup#hosts-vs-docker-dns (cc @new-hires) :book:
